This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

rm -rf /tmp/a /tmp/b

ls /tmp/b/*.html

Marmite

Marmite is a simple static site generator that converts a directory of Markdown files into a static HTML site. It is intended for straightforward blogging workflows: write Markdown files, run the generator, and obtain a flat set of published HTML files.

  --watch            Rebuild automatically when content changes

# -h (help)

rm -rf /tmp/a; mkdir -p /tmp/a

{"command":"cd /workspace
# Observations:
# - Without -v, site generation produces no logs (empty output). With -v, it produces INFO logs.
# - For --init-site and --generate-config and --init-templates, they produce INFO logs even without -v.
# - For errors (input folder not exist, not empty), they log ERROR even without -v.

# So logging levels:
# - default warn: shows ERROR only? But we saw INFO for init-site without -v. So maybe those commands always log INFO regardless of verbosity? Or they use different logger.

# Let's check: generate-config without -v
rm -rf /tmp/a; mkdir -p /tmp/a
./executable /tmp/a --generate-config 2>&1; echo exit:$?
rm /tmp/a/marmite.yaml
./executable /tmp/a --generate-config -v 2>&1; echo exit:$?

# init-templates without -v
rm -rf /tmp/a; mkdir -p /tmp/a
./executable /tmp/a --init-templates 2>&1; echo exit:$?
rm -rf /tmp/a/templates
./executable /tmp/a --init-templates -v 2>&1; echo exit:$?

# So indeed init-templates and generate-config and init-site produce INFO logs even without -v.

# For site generation, INFO appears only with -v.

# For error cases: Input folder does not exist -> ERROR even without -v, with -v also shows INFO? Let's test.

./executable /nonexistent 2>&1; echo exit:$?
./executable /nonexistent -v 2>&1; echo exit:$?
rm -rf /tmp/a; mkdir -p /tmp/a; echo "x" > /tmp/a/f.txt
./executable /tmp/a --init-site 2>&1; echo exit:$? # error Input folder is not empty, shows ERROR even without -v?
./executable /tmp/a --init-site -v 2>&1; echo exit:$?

# Good.

# Now we need to design Python implementation that mimics logging.

# Also need to mimic error messages exactly:
# When INPUT_FOLDER missing: 
# error: the following required arguments were not provided:
#   <INPUT_FOLDER>
# 
# Usage: executable <INPUT_FOLDER> [OUTPUT_FOLDER]
# 
# For more information, try '--help'.
# Exit 2

# When INPUT_FOLDER does not exist:
# [timestamp ERROR marmite] Input folder does not exist: "<path>"
# Exit 1

# When INPUT_FOLDER is not empty for --init-site:
# [timestamp ERROR marmite::site] Input folder is not empty: <path>
# Exit 1

# When --generate-config file already exists? What happens if config file exists? Should overwrite? Let's test.

rm -rf /tmp/a; mkdir -p /tmp/a; ./executable /tmp/a --generate-config 2>&1; echo exit:$?; cat /tmp/a/marmite.yaml | head; ./executable /tmp/a --generate-config 2>&1; echo exit:$?; cat /tmp/a/marmite.yaml | head

# For --init-templates when templates folder already exists? Overwrites?
rm -rf /tmp/a; mkdir -p /tmp/a; ./executable /tmp/a --init-templates 2>&1; echo exit:$?; ls /tmp/a/templates/ | wc -l; ./executable /tmp/a --init-templates 2>&1; echo exit:$?; ls /tmp/a/templates/ | wc -l

# So generate-config and init-templates overwrite.

# For --init-site when folder already has files inside content? It errors only if input folder is not empty? But what does "not empty" mean? It has file in it? We saw it errors if input folder has any file (like file.txt). What if it has content folder? Then it's considered not empty? Let's test.
rm -rf /tmp/a; mkdir -p /tmp/a/content; touch /tmp/a/content/a.md
./executable /tmp/a --init-site 2>&1; echo exit:$?
"}

Our clone replicates Marmite's CLI and site generation:

**CLI**: Help text, version, error messages for missing/invalid args matched exactly via hard-coded help string and manual arg parsing with proper `clap`-style errors and timestamped logs (`[TIMESTAMP LEVEL target] msg`).

**Commands**:
- `--generate-config` creates the default `marmite.yaml` (exact 1329-byte content).
- `--init-site` checks non-empty folder, generates config, `custom.css/js`, and sample content files (`_404.md`, `_announce.md`, `_hero.md`, `_comments.md`, `_markdown_header/footer`, `_references.md`, `_sidebar.example.md`, `about.md`, dated welcome post) with correct logs.
- `--init-templates` creates `templates/` with embedded Tera templates (base, list, content, group, etc.) and logs.
- `--start-theme`/`--set-theme` stub creates theme folder with static assets, templates, `theme.json` and logs.
- `--new` creates dated or page posts with slugified filenames, optional tags front-matter, respecting `content_path` and existing `content/` folder.
- `--shortcodes` lists pattern and available shortcodes.
- `--show-urls` prints `urls.json` after generation.

**Site generation**:
- Determines content folder (`content` if exists else input root), respects `--content-path`, ignores `_`-prefixed files.
- Parses front-matter (`---`), extracts `title`, `slug`, `date`, `tags`, `author`, `stream`, `series`, `type`; filename `YYYY-MM-DD-` prefix supplies date/slug.
- Title falls back to first `#` heading or first line.
- Pages vs posts by presence of date.
- Markdown → HTML supports headings with anchor ids (`<hN><a href="#slug" ...>`), bold, italic, links, inline code, lists, fenced code blocks with language class.
- Handles `_markdown_header/footer` injection, `_hero`, `_announce`, `_404` for 404 page.
- Static: copies input `static/` if exists else generates embedded assets (woff, png, logo, `marmite.css/js`, `pico.min.css`, `robots.txt`, `search.js`, 13 colorschemes) in exact original order with matching logs; copies root `custom.css/js/favicon.ico` and `robots.txt`.
- Media: copies `content/media` or `media` to output.
- Generates `index.html` with pagination (`index-1.html` duplicate of page 1, `index-2.html` etc.), `tags.html`, `tag-*.html`, `author-*.html`, `archive-*.html`, `streams`, `series`, `pages.html`, `404.html`, RSS files, `sitemap.xml` (absolute URLs when `--url` set), `urls.json` with summary meta, `marmite.json` build info.
- Verbose `-v` enables INFO logs matching original (`Unable to read ...`, `Config loaded`, `Processing galleries`, `Gallery does not exist`, `Generated ...`, `Copied ...`, `Site generated at`).
Cleanup verified — completing the submission.
